overall_summary: Analysis of 117 data points (representing 35 unique Shorts) reveals a strong viewer preference for extreme space anomalies and exoplanet facts, while cognitive psychology and brain-related facts consistently underperform. Longer Shorts (19-21 seconds) with high-contrast visual hooks (e.g., diamonds, rubies, dark coal) drive the highest engagement.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1,016 views) and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (721 views) consistently generate the highest views and engagement.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on extreme space facts, focusing on bizarre weather, planetary composition, and cosmic threats.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'Why Your Head Is Older Than Your Feet' (264 views) and 'Sharks Are Older Than Trees?' (302 views) perform moderately well compared to standard trivia.
winning_patterns.action: Incorporate physics-based anomalies that challenge common sense, using relatable reference points (like heads/feet or trees).

weak_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'Your Brain Is Hiding This From You' (38 views) and 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' (17 views) consistently fail to gain traction.
weak_patterns.action: Phase out standard cognitive psychology facts unless they can be framed with a high-stakes mystery hook.

weak_patterns.evidence: Re-uploading 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' multiple times resulted in extremely low views (5, 11, and 53 views).
weak_patterns.action: Avoid direct re-uploads of underperforming concepts; instead, pivot to entirely new topics or radically change the hook.

next_video.concept: The Planet Being Eaten Alive By Its Star (WASP-12b)
next_video.opening_direction: Right now, there is a pitch-black planet in our galaxy being slowly eaten alive by its own star.
next_video.twist_direction: The star's gravity is pulling the planet so hard it has warped into the shape of an egg, and it will be completely consumed in a few million years.
next_video.reason: Exoplanets with extreme conditions and dramatic visual narratives (like TrES-2b and the supersonic ruby planet) are the channel's top performers, pulling in 700-1000+ views. A 21-second duration aligns with the top-performing formats.

experiment: Test a 'What-If' cinematic scenario combining space and geography, such as 'What If a Black Hole Entered Our Solar System?' or 'What If the Moon Was Replaced by Jupiter?' with high-quality AI-generated cinematic visuals to see if the space audience converts to high-retention visual storytelling.
